name: Ereğli
title: Ereğli Ship Gauging: UTM for Steel-Trade Bulk Carriers
description: Ship thickness gauging at Ereğli on Turkey's Black Sea coast: ultrasonic UTM for bulk carriers and steel-trade cargo ships at the steelworks port or at anchor.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships Calling at Karadeniz Ereğli
intro: Ereğli is a steel town on Turkey's Black Sea coast, and its port exists to serve the integrated steelworks behind it. Bulk carriers arrive with iron ore and coal and sail with steel products, so the ships are mostly Handysize to Panamax tonnage working a hard cargo programme. Atlantis sends technicians from India to the vessel for each job, and the gauging is planned around discharge sequences, loading windows and the anchorage waits that the coast's weather imposes.

highlights.p: Iron ore and coal come in, coils, slabs and plate go out. That cycle works holds hard, and abrasion and corrosion of hold frames, hopper plating and tank-top plating are exactly what thickness measurement is asked to size.
Grab discharge of ore and coal empties holds one after another over days. As each hold is cleaned and declared safe, frames and bulkheads can be gauged without pulling the ship off its berth.
Heavy repair for Black Sea bulkers usually happens in the Marmara yards. Readings taken at Ereğli let a superintendent send yards a measured steel scope before the ship makes the passage.

port.h: Ereğli: a steelworks port on the western Black Sea
p: Karadeniz Ereğli sits on the western Black Sea coast of Turkey, between Istanbul and Zonguldak, on an open shoreline with no natural harbour of any size. The port was built to serve the steelworks, and its breakwaters shelter a handful of berths where raw materials are discharged and finished products are shipped. Ships approach from the open sea, so swell and onshore winds matter more here than in a river or fjord port, and berthing slots are sometimes lost to weather in the winter months. Anchorage areas lie off the coast for ships waiting for a berth.

The traffic is dominated by dry bulk. Iron ore and coking coal arrive from the Black Sea, the Mediterranean and further afield, usually in Handysize, Supramax and Panamax bulk carriers, and the outbound trade is steel in the form of coils, slabs, plate and long products, carried by bulkers and general cargo ships with strengthened tank tops and large hatch openings. Because the cargo is dense and abrasive, ships calling here tend to show wear in the lower hold frames, the tank top, the hopper plating and the hatch cover and coaming structure, which is where gauging attention is usually concentrated.

The same ships often continue to other Black Sea and Marmara ports in a single voyage, and many are older vessels in regional trades whose owners watch their steel condition closely. Ereğli therefore sees both owner-driven condition gauging between cargoes and programmes timed to a coming special survey. There is no large commercial drydock at Ereğli itself for ocean-going ships, so the port's role in an inspection plan is usually early evidence, taken while the ship is discharging, that feeds a docking decision made elsewhere on the Turkish coast.

facilities.h: Where a ship can be gauged at Ereğli
p: At the steelworks berths, gauging follows the cargo operation. Holds are gauged one at a time as the grabs finish and the cleaning gang has swept the tank top, with the ship's crew preparing ventilation, lighting and safe access in advance and the master issuing the enclosed-space entry permit for each space. A bulk carrier that stays several days discharging can usually take a complete programme of frames, bulkheads and hatch coamings in that time, while a quick ore or coal discharge may support only a few holds. Access to the berths follows the port's own ISPS rules and is booked through the ship's agent.

When berths are occupied, ships wait at anchor off the coast. Those waits can be long enough for deck work, hatch cover panels and coamings, ballast tank readings and, where the holds are empty, hold structure. Boarding is by launch and is weather-dependent, so the programme is ordered with the highest-priority areas first. For a full docking-grade scope, owners generally plan the work in a yard in the Marmara, and the Ereğli readings become the preliminary steel estimate.
list: Steelworks bulk berths — hold frame, bulkhead and tank-top gauging on bulk carriers during grab discharge of ore and coal
Steel product berths — hatch cover, coaming and hold checks on general cargo ships and bulkers taking coils, slabs and plate
Outer anchorage off the coast — deck, hatch cover and ballast tank gauging on ships waiting for a berth, reached by launch
Ballast tank access during cargo work — topside, hopper and double-bottom tanks measured once emptied, ventilated and certified safe
Pre-docking checks before a Marmara yard call — an early steel list for the superintendent, built from readings taken in hold and tank

context.h: Black Sea trade, port state control and what drives inspection here
p: Turkey is a member of both the Black Sea MoU and the Mediterranean MoU, and bulk carriers on regional trades are regularly inspected under port state control. Structural condition is a recurring theme with older bulkers: wasted hatch coamings, corroded air pipe heads and wasting in hold frames are the sort of findings that lead a manager to commission gauging before the next inspection finds it first. Turkish-flag and Turkish-managed bulk tonnage is classed with a mix of international societies and the national society, and superintendents usually work to the class's own thickness measurement report format.

The Black Sea is outside the Mediterranean emission control area, so ships calling at Ereğli face the global fuel limit rather than the 0.10% area limit, although ships that continue into the Sea of Marmara cross into the ECA. For vessels that will later trade to European Union ports, the EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires a current Inventory of Hazardous Materials, and voyages touching EU ports bring EU ETS reporting. These rules do not change how steel is measured, but they do shape how owners decide when to dock a ship and how much steel work to put into it.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Ereğli
jobs.p: Work at Ereğli follows the steel cycle. A bulk carrier discharging ore or coal gives access to holds in sequence, a ship loading steel gives a shorter and busier window for hatch covers and decks, and a ship at anchor gives time for tanks. Most programmes are scoped by the superintendent as a preparation for a special or intermediate survey, a sale, or a charterer's inspection, and readings are sent to the technical department as each area is finished.
list: Hold frame, hopper and tank-top gauging on a Supramax bulk carrier discharging coking coal ahead of its third special survey in a Marmara yard.
Hatch cover panel, coaming and cross-deck gauging on a Handysize general cargo ship loading steel coils, to confirm which items need renewal at the next docking.
Ballast tank gauging on a Panamax bulker waiting at anchor for a berth, giving the owner's technical department an early view of topside and hopper tank condition.
Pre-purchase condition gauging of an older bulk carrier at the discharge berth, with the buyer's superintendent attending and holds opened for inspection.
Magnetic particle checks of hatch-corner and frame-bracket welds on a bulk carrier after cracking was reported at the same details on a sister ship.

logistics: The nearest international airports are in Istanbul, with Sabiha Gökçen on the Anatolian side the more convenient for the coast road east, though the journey to Ereğli is by road and depends on traffic. Port passes at the steelworks berths and launches for anchorage work are arranged through the ship's agent, with crew lists and certificates sent in advance. Turkey requires a visa for Indian passport holders, so we begin the application once a call is likely and keep the validity covering the ship's expected window, which can shift with weather and berthing.

faqs.q: Can holds be gauged while the ship is discharging iron ore or coal?
faqs.a: Yes, one hold at a time. Once the grabs have finished a hold and the cleaning gang has swept the tank top, the master can issue the entry permit and we gauge frames, bulkheads and plating. Holds still being worked are left until later. The superintendent agrees the order of holds with us so that the most worn areas are measured first.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Ereğli for a renewal survey?
faqs.a: Not for ocean-going bulk carriers. Owners usually dock in the Marmara region or at a yard elsewhere on the Turkish coast. What Ereğli offers is the chance to take readings during cargo work, so the steel estimate is ready before the ship reaches the yard and the yard can order plate and plan the work earlier.

faqs.q: What can be done if the ship has to wait at anchor off Ereğli?
faqs.a: A wait for berth is useful time. Deck plating, hatch covers, coamings and ballast tanks that the crew have prepared can be gauged, and empty holds can be measured if they are safe to enter. Boarding is by launch and depends on sea conditions, so we agree a priority list and measure the key areas first.

faqs.q: Do winter conditions on the Black Sea coast affect gauging?
faqs.a: They can. Swell and strong onshore winds may delay launches at the anchorage and disturb berthing slots, and cold weather makes outdoor work on deck slower. Inside holds and tanks the conditions are steadier. We build slack into the plan and move interior work forward when deck work is not possible.
